name: Very Special Oval Georgian Studio
description: Experience authentic Georgian elegance is this unique large OVAL studio apartment, overlooking park.  Accommodates two in cosy sleeping loft. Cook dinner in the designer kitchen, and then head out to enjoy the attractions of the city.
neighborhood_overview:
A beautiful, historic residential square, built in 1790's, within 5-10 minutes walk of down-town city centre. Elegance and convenience combined with a bit of inner city grittiness. I have loved it all, since 1978!

Mountjoy Square is situated just NE of the historic city centre, within walking distance of just about all the main city attractions. It is the most densely populated area in the entire city: 1500 people have front doors opening onto the Square.

The house fronts onto a 4acre/1.5ha park, across a fairly busy street. This apartment faces the side street, so it is quieter, but you will still hear traffic.....Please bear in mind that this is NOT LEAFY SUBURBIA, but a vibrant, living city community and it's definitely gritty in places... Having said that, I have lived here, uneventfully, for nearly 38 years, and consider the trade-offs well worth it, for the excitement and convenience of having the city on my doorstep..
host_about: Architectural enthusiast & committed urbanite, Alexander technique teacher, daily swimmer. I love to cook and to share meals with friends, and I aspire  to grow at least some of my own food. I love where I live, and enjoy all the amenities the city has to offer. I am Secretary of the Mountjoy Square Society, whose aim is to improve our area for all who live work and visit here. I am also a committee member of the Irish Georgian Society, and I regularly organize  day trips and walking tours for our members.

Rathmines (Irish: Ráth Maonais, meaning 'ringfort of Maonas') is an inner suburb on the Southside of Dublin in Ireland.
It lies three kilometres south of the city centre. It begins at the southern side of the Grand Canal and stretches along the Rathmines Road as far as Rathgar to the south, Ranelagh to the east, and Harold's Cross to the west.
It is situated in the city's D06 postal district.

Rathmines is served by the Luas light rail system: Ranelagh on the Green Line is the most convenient for access to the main street, while the Charlemont and Beechwood stops are also within walking distance of the area.

Dublin Bus routes 14, 15, 15A, 15B, 18, 65, 65B, 83, 140 and 142 serve Rathmines. The area is also served by the Dublin Bus Nitelink routes 15N and 49N on Friday and Saturday nights and on public holidays.

Sullivan street was one of the first developments by the Guinness family to provide housing for employees in the 1890's. It's the archetypal Dublin red brick terrace that is very central and alive with city living.

Phoenix Park – the largest in-city park in the world – is literally on your doorstep, and is also home to Dublin Zoo. Dublin’s biggest tourist attraction – the Guinness Storehouse – is a few minutes walk, as well as other big names such as the Jameson Distillery, the Irish Museum of Modern Art and the Four Courts.

The area is friendly and tranquil, and with one of Dublin's universities nestled in multiple locations around the area, there is plenty of live and energy to the neighborhood. Just a 20-minute walk to O'Connell Street and a short drive to Dublin Airport.

Drumcondra is well serviced by public transport and it's very easy to hail a taxi. Attractions include Croke Park stadium, where Ireland's national games of Gaelic football and hurling may be seen - boasting a capacity for 82,000 people, it is one of the largest sports stadiums in Europe. The National Botanic Gardens have restored Victorian glasshouses, and Glasnevin Cemetery includes museum exhibits on Irish historical figures buried there.

name: Fab Dublin City Apt near Dublin Castle,Guinness SH
description: Treat yourself & stay at my remodelled spacious apartment arranged with luxurious comfort, convenience & free wifi. Immerse yourself in the historical district. Staying close to ChristChurch, you are at the cultural heart, flanked by Dublin Castle, St. Patrick's & the Guinness Storehouse, Jameson Distillery, Vicar Street venue minutes away. Temple Bar, Smock Alley, Trinity College, Museums, Grafton Street shops, all a short walk away. Come make memories here, they'll last a lifetime.
neighborhood_overview: This is the historical part of Dublin, so you will be spoiled for choice. Dublinia is beside Christchurch and is a historical recreation museum, concentrating on Viking and medieval history of the city.  The Guinness Storehouse is well worth a visit.  Dublin Castle is 5 mins away, built in the 13th century.  Of course, Trinity College, Temple Bar, and the shopping area of Grafton Street are just a 10 to 15 minute stroll down through Dame Street passing the Olympia Theatre as you go.  Self hire Dublin bikes are available at Wood Quay, Christchurch Place, should you like to tour Dublin by bike.  In that case I would recommend a ride up to the Phoenix Park, one of the largest Public Parks in Europe and so beautiful, you might catch sight of a deer or a stag.  The Phoenix Park is about a 20 minutes walk, and if you like to get a run in on your break, you would certainly enjoy the sights here.
host_about:
Hello! Why does the idea of talking about oneself strike fear in one's heart, is it that we're just too bashful or the subject matter might be boring, ha.  I'm a mother of two wonderful young adults. I took up running some years ago and have ran many International Marathons including some of the majors New York, Boston, London, Paris, San Francisco all of which I qualified for where necessary.  I'm a glass half full type of person and certainly believe that if plan A doesn't work, there's always plan B, C, etc.,.  I enjoy meeting people and hosting with Airbnb has been a terrific experience for me in that regard.  In general I love to see people enjoying life and if I can help them in that goal, all the better.  I'm a believer in karma and thus each day is an opportunity to do something good and make people happy.  Of course , I have a huge work ethic and I like to give a 100% to whatever I'm working on.  I'm a  cleanliness freak, having had a bad experience in what I thought was a good hotel in London, long story short, I jumped into bed after a long day in London and a late theatre night, in the morning when I woke, I noticed there was a brown coffee stain on my sheet, obviously the sheets had not been changed, I was Not a happy camper!  Who would have thought, needless to say, I check wherever I stay now!   
I love Dublin city and the people, I'm a Dubliner even though my Dad hailed from County Kerry (the California of Ireland), and my Mum from County Westmeath.  I love to pretend to be a tourist in my own city, the things you notice and discover, always something new.  Life always has moments to be recorded, thus the advent of phones with cameras has enabled me to embrace my other passion, photography, I think I have at least 20,000 photos,  thank goodness for iCloud.
Hope all that didn't bore you too much, have a wonderful day, Namaste.:-)

It's a very "studenty" part of town being very near to DCU and the Mater Hospital. This means there are plenty of good small restaurants and convenience stores all around.

neighborhood_overview: Howth is an idyllic fishing village on the northeast of Dublin and has been immortalised in James Joyce’s Ulysses. The medieval ruins of St. Mary’s Abbey lie nearby.  A clifftop trail has sweeping sea views, indeed H.G. Wells once remarked that Howth had "the finest views west of Naples". neighborhood_overview:
The Liberties is considered by many the heart of Dublin as well as being home to the world-famous and Ireland’s most visited tourist attraction – Guinness!

In medieval times Dublin was a walled city with tariffs and taxes charged to protect the city. However, The Liberties, was located just outside the city walls of Norman Dublin making its residents at liberty from the city laws, including the need to pay taxes!

Later, the area became home to a large French Hugenot population along with crafts such as weavers and whiskey distillers.

During the late 18th and 19th century, The Liberties was full of breweries and distilleries, including the Guinness family, who built the now famous site at St James’ Gate in 1759.

Today, it’s Ireland’s most visited tourist attraction and it’s just c400m from the apartment! Meanwhile a recent renaissance in whiskey distillers in The Liberties means there are plenty for whiskey lovers.

description:
Our family home is in a secluded cul de sac in Raheny village, close to all shops, pubs, restaurants and amenities Raheny and the surrounding areas have to offer.
We want you to enjoy your stay with us so have made every effort to make your room warm, quiet and comfortable. You also have access to the living areas, gardens and kitchen facilities should you wish to have a quiet night in.

neighborhood_overview:
Our home is in historic Raheny Village which is on the coast about 8km (5.0 mi) from Dublin city center and 7km (4.3 mi) from Dublin Airport.
For music and sports fans, the Three Arena is just 7km away, Croke Park Stadium 6km and the Aviva rugby stadium less than 10km.
Two major features of Raheny are the 5 km (3.1 mi) beach known as Dollymount Strand on the nature reserve of Bull Island, and Saint Annes, the largest of Dublin's municipal parks, formerly the home of the Gunness family.
Eight crescent cottages on Station Road near the junction with the Howth Road are among the oldest buildings in the village, having been built around 1790.
There is excellent walking and cycling on the sea front, the Bull Island, in St. Anne's Park and around the local streets.
For golfers, we have the Royal Dublin, Portmarnock, Clontarf and St. Annes Golf Clubs all on our doorstep, with many more close by.

description:
Walk right or left (5 - 10 mins) and you will be on a promenade, each with a different view. Further 5 mins and you will be on Burrow beach, Sutton, Dublin 13 or taking in the view over Dublin Bay at the Marine Hotel. We moved here to get the best of both - coastal living with near/quick/late night public transport to the City and Airport (taxi) - 20 mins, Howth marina/wkend market/hill/cafes/restaurants & pubs.
Malahide castle and marina.
We hope you'll stay and see the benefits as we do.
neighborhood_overview:
Our road/area is quiet/tidy with good reputation and there is a small shop/garage just around the corner on Baldoyle Road which is open early to late. Also, Elphin pub/food/some live music, Pizza and Chinese takeaways.
Baldoyle has Lidl, White House pub and restaurant and the Library.
Sutton Cross is 5 minutes away and the heart of Sutton. Here you will find a variety of small restaurants, coffee shops, food shops, tennis club. Marine Hotel, (lots of brochures at reception), has back exit to sit and view Dublin Bay, the Dinghy club and passing ships. There are dedicated cycling and walking routes along the bay and hill and cliff walks. . Nearby there are 2 golf courses (Sutton and Deer Park). Burrow beach is a Must see for views and maybe walk along the beach to Howth. (Watch Tide - strong currents).
Howth is a charming village with pubs and restaurants famous for their live Irish music entertainment and food, (seafood).

description:

neighborhood_overview:
The oldest settled area of Dublin, Chapelizod still feels like a village, bordered by the River Liffey and the Park and with a strong sense of community. There are three top pubs within 100 m of the house: The Villager for music, Mullingar House for good food (best chicken wings in Ireland!) and the Bridge Gastropub. Baa baa's Cafe 5 doors down. Why we are here?

Hotels aren't always hip and hosts aren't always reliable so we’ve spotted a gap where we filter out all the crap. We want to change the game with unique spaces that inspire and that can be remarkable and affordable at the same time.

The Hiphipstay story started back in 2015 when our founder Will McGlade was travelling around the US with his mates. During their travels, vacation rentals were always their first choice over hotels. They loved the added comfort of renting a home in a city or a coastal town and living like a local.

How we got started ?

Will recognised a gap in the homestay market back home Ireland. He wanted to put an end to having to trawl through hundreds of average listings to find something special. So he created a platform that made it simple to rent the absolute best homes available, where hotel meets home.

Where we’re going ?

What began as a journey to provide a better stay has grown into a celebration of modern design and exceptional comfort. We’re working with world-class software developers, hosts and designers to create truly remarkable spaces—ones that transcend hospitality and enrich lives to bring Hiphipstay to be a truly global brand.

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome to the enchanting realm of Howth, a hidden gem that defies its mere 25-minute train ride from the city centre. This village, adorned with a picturesque harbour, charming beaches, and sea cliffs adorned in a vibrant tapestry of wildflowers, transports you to a distant haven along the western coast.

As you step into this coastal haven, the waterfront promenade invites you to a mesmerising dance with nature. Keep an eye out for the whimsical resident seals, their playful heads peeking between the embrace of docked boats, as if sharing a secret with the sea breeze. It's this ethereal connection to the marine world that beckons Dubliners seeking a weekend respite, a breath of untamed ocean air that awakens the soul.

Beyond its captivating allure, Howth holds the promise of a perfect day-trip sanctuary. The shoreline is adorned with a string of exceptional seafood restaurants, a symphony of flavours that pay homage to the maritime embrace. Embark on cliff walks

neighborhood_overview:
This is an old traditional "working class" part of town. The houses are cosy and functional - all built in the 1920's. It's famous for the huge Croke Park stadium - the home of the GAA - which hosts 2 big concerts most years and of course many matches most weekends.

It's a very "studenty" part of town being very near to DCU and the Mater Hospital. This means there are plenty of good small restaurants and convenience stores all around.

For a pleasant walk I may recommend the Canal (up by the statue of Brendan Behan) or a great walk via Griffith Park to the Botanic Gardens and onwards to Glasnevin Cemetery.

Drumcondra (as the area is known) was the stomping ground of Bertie Ahern if you're interested in that sort of thing.

Coffee shops and breakfast haunts are filled with atmosphere. I love the little French café where early risers sip over their morning coffee. There is lots to see and do in my area among all the famous sites there are plenty of cute cafes, award winning restaurants, gastro pubs and wet pubs.

Alfresco morning breakfast at the Queen of Tarts on Cows lane, where I often read the morning paper with a sweet treat and tea from a china cup. Afternoon croissant on the heated terrace of the Castle gates.

My favourite family friendly Itali

name: Contemporary family home in beautiful Howth
description: Our comfy spacious family home is available to rent this summer. Located on a quiet, leafy cul de sac with a beautiful sandy beach 200m from the door. It’s a 10 minute walk into Howth Village, famous for its many fish restaurants, beautiful cliff walks and beaches. You can rent a kayak, take an off-road bike tour, visit a puffin colony on an uninhabited island all within this small peninsula just a 20 minute journey from Dublin City Centre.
neighborhood_overview:
The house is ideally located, with access to a sandy beach 200m from the door. From here you can walk into Howth or further on to burrow beach if the sea is far enough out. At high tide the beach is largely inaccessible so you may have it all to yourself!

Howth is a gorgeous spot, the village is famous for its seafood restaurants and there is a lovely buzz about the place with many people sitting outside enjoying food and a glass of wine. There are a couple of small museums, a playground and some boutique shops. There are often lots of visitors out walking the pier with a coffee and soaking up the views.

For walking fans the coastline offers a varied mix of cliffs, pebbly beaches and lots of sand, plus there are nice treks through old woods in the middle of the peninsula to summits with views over many counties (and on a good day you can even see Wales!)

There are a variety of water sports on offer - kayaking, yachting, diving, stand up paddle board....
host_about:
Originally from the UK I’ve been living in Ireland for the last 12 years. I love where we live and Howth is now very much home for myself, hubby and our three small children. Pre kids we loved to travel the world, our trips now are less exotic but we still love a change of scenery now and then.

We are blessed with a fab house and are happy to be able to share it with others who can enjoy the house and the area whilst we’re away ourselves.

name: Authentic Dublin Experience in Stunning Location
description:
Stunning historic location on the Liffey quays, with a knowledgeable and friendly host.

Traditional scones and homecooked breakfasts included. Main sights within 15 mins walk! Bordering Smithfield Square with artisan cafes, bars, restaurants, cinema and supermarkets. Jameson Distillery a 3 minute walk, as is the ancient Brazen Head pub (join us for our traditional music sessions!)

neighborhood_overview:
Living on "the quays" (the walled river banks through the centre of Dublin) at Smithfield has been a joy since I moved to Dublin from Galway after university.

This is exactly where the original crossing place of the river Liffey grew into the town we call Dublin. Across the river is the Brazen Head, Ireland's oldest pub, while the Jameson whiskey distillery is almost next door.

Smithfield Square is outside our gate, with its artisan cafes and many restaurants, and when the breeze blows the right direction, you can smell the malt/coffee scent of Guinness barley being roasted, or hear the bells of Christchurch Cathedral.

Even from the window of your bright riverfront bedroom you can watch swans glide past, see a stork fishing from the Quay wall below, or, if you're lucky, see our seal (!!) swim past as the tide turns and he gets the opportunity to catch some freshwater fish!

description:
Step inside a storybook slice of old Ireland.

Biddy’s Cottage is a lovingly preserved 19th-century fisherman’s home perched above Coliemore Harbour.

This self-catering stay blends authentic heritage with quiet comfort. Features include a turf fireplace, whitewashed stone walls, a contempory kitchen, traditional Irish decor, and quaint Coliemore Harbour and the sea just steps from the front door.

Relax by the hearth, cook with fresh market finds, or wander Dalkey’s cafes, walks and coves.
neighborhood_overview:
Tucked between sea and hill, Dalkey is one of Dublin’s most picturesque and storied villages. Once a Viking settlement and medieval port, today it blends old-world charm with easygoing luxury. Wander its winding lanes and you’ll find artisan cafés, independent bookshops, traditional pubs with live music, and restaurants known well beyond the village.

The coastline is just minutes away — ideal for sea swims, coastal walks, or simply watching the seals basking by Coliemore Harbour. From there, you can hop on a boat to Dalkey Island, home to ancient ruins and wild goats.

Behind the village rises Killiney Hill Park, where forested paths lead to panoramic views across Dublin Bay to Howth and, on a clear day, the mountains of Wales.

Dalkey is peaceful but well connected — only 25 minutes to the city centre by DART. Locals greet you by name, yet some of Ireland’s best-known artists, writers, and musicians call it home.

There is more than 700 hectares to explore and not only does the the President of Ireland live there in "The Aras", but it's also home to Dublin Zoo, has play grounds for the kids, polo and cricket grounds, cycle paths and bike rental, coffee shops, as well as a large herd of fallow deer that still call it home.
Stoneybatter is your local neighbourhood for hanging out in. Situated on the Northside of the River Liffey, it's one of the last genuine inner city urban villages, where old Dublin meets new development, but still has a strong community spirit and a local feel. Manor Street has become a foodie hub shared with artists and crafters and can boast its own publishing house and bookshop, Liliput Press (their namesake coffee and deli should not be missed!)
Parkgate Street is a 6 minute walk for your immediate shopping

Nowadays though, life is different, we have 3 small children so we rarely get past the front door without a bit of effort. That's why we would like to make our home (or spare room) available to people who want to explore Dublin - we can get a bit of the travelling experience from our visitors! We both like movies and books, box sets of Sopranos, The Wire (and a little bit of Downton just for me) and, of course, Guinness. I hope to provide a guest with a welcoming atmosphere, interesting chat and good ideas about how to get the most out of their stay in Dublin, whatever their age or interests.

description: Set in a quiet neighbourhood, our home is our happy place! Our style is a bit different from the average Irish decor, and we like it that way! It's largely residential, and it’s only a quick bus, taxi, cycle, or walk into the heart of the city (for reference, Trinity College is 5km/3mi and the Guiness Storehouse is 3.5km/2.25mi!). Shops and buses are within a two-minute walk from the front door.

Why we are here?

Hotels aren't always hip and hosts aren't always reliable so we’ve spotted a gap where we filter out all the crap. We want to change the game with unique spaces that inspire and that can be remarkable and affordable at the same time.

The Hiphipstay story started back in 2015 when our founder Will McGlade was travelling around the US with his mates. During their travels, vacation rentals were always their first choice over hotels. How we got started ?

Will recognised a gap in the homestay market back home Ireland. He wanted to put an end to having to trawl through hundreds of average listings to find something special. So he created a platform that made it simple to rent the absolute best homes available, where hotel meets home.

Where we’re going ?

What began as a journey to provide a better stay has grown into a celebration of modern design and exceptional comfort. A short stroll brings you into Ringsend, a lively riverside area with cafés, bakeries and more pubs, as well as the Grand Canal Dock district with its theatres, restaurants and modern waterfront vibe.

Head the other direction and you reach Sandymount, a leafy village with a green at its centre and the wide, sandy strand stretching for miles. Locals come here for walks by the sea and coffee afterwards in one of the many cafés.

neighborhood_overview:
Grand Canal Street Lower in Dublin is a lively area where the charm of old-world canals meets the energy of a modern city. The street runs alongside the historic Grand Canal, offering a scenic backdrop of locks, bridges, and swans that contrasts beautifully with trendy cafés, artisan bakeries, and boutique businesses lining the road. Its blend of local character and contemporary lifestyle makes it a favourite for both Dubliners and visitors seeking an authentic yet vibrant atmosphere.

Just a short walk away is Grand Canal Dock, often dubbed "Silicon Docks" for its mix of global tech offices and modern architecture. The area features the striking Bord Gáis Energy Theatre, contemporary public squares, and waterside promenades that host everything from food markets to open-air performances. Grand Canal Street Lower is a dynamic gateway into the city’s urban and creative pulse with cultural landmarks, relaxed dining spots, and easy access to central Dublin.
